s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive retinal vascular proliferation with macular edema resolution
salient_findings: Macular edema resolution after intravitreal anti-VEGF injections
Hyperreflective tissues proliferating on retinal vessels on OCTA
Dendritic vascular-like structures on Fluorescein Angiography
key_facts: 76-year-old woman presented with macular edema
Treated with 2 intravitreal anti-VEGF injections
Macular edema completely resolved at 3 months
No recurrence of macular edema
OCTA findings at 6 months showed no abnormality
OCTA findings at 12 months showed hyperreflective tissues on retinal vessels
OCTA findings at 15 months showed increased hyperreflective tissues with angiogenic sprouts
OCTA findings at 18 months showed development in area of preexisting proliferation
OCTA findings at 21 months showed enlarged horizontal structures along retina surface
Fluorescein Angiography at 21 months showed dendritic vascular-like structures

shortlist.label: Retinal angiomatous proliferation
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of progressive retinal vascular proliferation with macular edema resolution

shortlist.label: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the patient's age and the development of neovascularization

shortlist.label: Retinal vascular proliferation
shortlist.why_kept: Directly related to the observed progression of retinal vascular changes

shortlist.label: Choroidal neovascularization
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of the neovascularization and macular edema

shortlist.label: Idiopathic juxtafoveolar retinal telangiectasis
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the development of abnormal vascular structures in the retina
